content.title: About
content.content: Cooked onions are peeled onion bulbs that have been boiled until tender. Heat softens the texture, reduces sharpness and brings out a natural sweetness. They are a common ingredient in soups, sauces, stews and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions belong to the Amaryllidaceae family and are close relatives of garlic, shallots and leeks.
Cooking destroys many of the volatile compounds that cause tears when cutting raw onions.
Cooked onions are featured in classic dishes worldwide, such as French onion soup, Indian pakoras and Japanese nikujaga.
Heat converts some of the onion’s sugars, making the flavor sweeter.
When stored in an airtight container, cooked onions keep in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cooked onions retain quercetin and sulfur compounds that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Sulfur compounds may help lower cholesterol and improve blood vessel function.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Although some vitamin C is lost during heating, cooked onions still provide a modest amount of this immune‑supporting vitamin.

items.title: May aid blood‑sugar regulation
items.content: Phytochemicals in onions can improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Promotes digestive health
items.content: The fiber in onions supports regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions, ranging from skin itching to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Onions contain fructans, which can cause gas and bloating in sensitive people.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: If cooked in salted water, the added sodium should be considered in the overall diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add cooked onions to soups, sauces, purees, salads, casseroles and pie fillings. They also make a tasty topping for meat or fish. For extra flavor, briefly sauté the cooked onions before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool cooked onions to room temperature, then place them in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags – they retain quality for about 3 months.
